source.title: Global Low-Rank, Local Full-Rank: The Holographic Encoding of Learned Algorithms

record.tranche_reason: The study measures grokking outcomes under modular-arithmetic training and sweeps weight decay, using different analyses from the original studies. It does not reproduce their detailed train/test accuracy trajectories.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that all 15 conditions reach mean test accuracy above 97%, and gives grokking-step counts for a few settings. It does not report when training accuracy saturates or sweep training-set size. Its trajectory-PCA and static-SVD reconstruction results concern the structure and compressibility of grokked solutions, not the gradual formation of a generalizing circuit or removal of memorizing components. Those results are not recorded as rows for the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The paper uses grokked multi-task modular-arithmetic Transformers as a substrate. Its results concern how compressible the final solutions are: trajectory PCA versus per-matrix and joint SVD reconstruction, plus activation-space selectivity. The grokking facts it states are setup descriptions, with training dynamics deferred to Xu (2026c). They give no training-accuracy saturation time, no pre-transition test accuracy, no accuracy curves and no training-set-size sweep, so they cannot show a delay after memorization. The weight-decay speed-up in grokking steps is not V5's efficiency account, critical dataset size or ungrokking. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that grokked solutions are globally low-rank in trajectory space (3–5 PCs recover >95% accuracy) but locally full-rank within weight matrices, and they call this the holographic encoding principle. They also note that stronger weight decay speeds grokking and makes the trunk less compressible by per-matrix SVD.
record.recipe_differences: Multi-task addition, multiplication, and quadratic operations modulo 97; shared-trunk Transformers; analysis focuses on trajectory PCA and per-matrix/joint SVD reconstruction rather than reproducing the original training-accuracy and test-accuracy measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking time changes with weight decay and model size; the paper reports the baseline-model comparison between λ = 0.1 and 1.0 and a 6,400-step result for the large model at λ = 1.0.

fits_no_version.finding: In multi-task modular arithmetic (mod 97, 50/50 split, AdamW full-batch), higher weight decay shortens the time to reach >95% test accuracy: baseline model ~157K steps at λ=0.1 versus ~25K at λ=1.0; large model 6,400 steps at λ=1.0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stronger weight decay shortens time-to-generalize in grokking on modular arithmetic.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokked trunk weights can be reconstructed to >95% accuracy from 2–6 trajectory PCs, yet per-matrix SVD at rank 64 and joint SVD at half rank fail (near chance in many conditions). Higher weight decay lowers rank-64 per-matrix reconstruction accuracy from ~70% to ~5%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokked solutions are low-dimensional in trajectory space but effectively full-rank per weight matrix.

record.problems: For the grokking claim, the paper does not provide training-accuracy trajectories, a training-set-size sweep, or uncertainty estimates for the reported grokking times. The study is limited to multi-task modular arithmetic in relatively small Transformers.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's trajectory-PC reconstruction, per-matrix and joint SVD reconstruction, activation-space selectivity, and subspace-overlap findings were not entered as rows because they do not measure a behavior named by the claim versions. The paper also reports condition-specific reconstruction tables and figures (Tables 2–6 and Figures 1–3); these address the paper's encoding/compression question rather than the tested grokking claims.

untested.parts: Test accuracy at chance before the jump, timing of training-accuracy saturation, shape of the transition, and how the delay depends on training-set size (fixed 50/50 split).

Gradual formation of a Fourier circuit, later removal of memorizing components, and progress measures that anticipate the jump. Trajectory PCs are analysed only for reconstructing the final model; the link of PC1–2 to Fourier features is asserted, not measured.
Non-algorithmic data, initialization scale, weight norm, and the lazy-to-rich transition.
LLM pretraining or fine-tuning; the paper only speculates about emergence in LLMs.
Circuit efficiency versus memorization, a critical dataset size, and ungrokking.
Whether different runs or architectures learn the same algorithm.
Controls for optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax limits.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its supports labels for V1 and V5 are not warranted. Every grokking fact in the paper is a setup statement, and the dynamics are delegated to the author's companion paper (Xu 2026c). Reaching high test accuracy says nothing about delay without a training-saturation time. A weight-decay speed-up is compatible with V5 but does not test its efficiency or critical-dataset-size predictions. The record's version statuses for V1 and V5 should be changed to not_tested.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report training accuracy saturation, test accuracy at chance before grokking, accuracy curves establishing the shape of the transition, or a training-set-size sweep.

It reconstructs final models from trajectory PCs but does not track formation of a generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or whether continuous progress measures anticipate a test-accuracy jump.
It does not test non-algorithmic data, initialization scale, weight norm, or a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.

The paper reports grokking times across weight-decay settings, but does not test whether a more efficient generalizing circuit displaces memorization, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
It does not compare algorithms learned across runs or test whether the same identifiable algorithm is reached under different architectures or hyperparameters.
It does not control for adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax limits, or test whether controlling them removes grokking.

rows.subject: all 15 conditions (3 model scales × 5 weight decay settings)
rows.operation_detail: Train shared-trunk Transformers on three modular-arithmetic tasks until all tasks grok or the maximum step count is reached.
rows.value: All 15 conditions achieve full grokking (mean test accuracy >97%); the stopping criterion is test accuracy >95% on all three tasks.
rows.note: Reports successful high test accuracy, but not the prior training-accuracy saturation or a chance-level-to-near-perfect test-accuracy trajectory.
rows.check: This is the stopping criterion and a final-accuracy outcome (all conditions >97% test accuracy), essentially a selection/setup value. With no training-accuracy saturation time or pre-jump test accuracy, it cannot show V1's delayed jump.

rows.subject: Baseline model
rows.operation_detail: Train with AdamW at the stated weight decay until grokking.
rows.note: The paper reports the step count but not the training-accuracy saturation time or the intervening accuracy trajectory.
rows.check: It reports steps to reach >95% test accuracy (~157K at λ=0.1), but not when training accuracy saturated, so the delay cannot be read. It does not bear on V5's efficiency, critical-dataset-size or ungrokking predictions.

rows.subject: Baseline model
rows.operation_detail: Train with AdamW at the stated weight decay until grokking.
rows.note: The paper says higher weight decay accelerates grokking; this comparison does not establish the proposed efficiency mechanism.
rows.check: Higher weight decay shortens time to grok (~25K vs ~157K steps). This does not measure the delay after memorization (V1) and does not test V5's mechanism or predictions; it is better recorded under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Large model
rows.operation_detail: Train with AdamW at the stated weight decay until grokking.
rows.note: The paper gives no corresponding large-model timing at another weight decay in this passage.
rows.check: This is a single grokking-step count (6,400 steps, large model, λ=1.0) with no training-saturation time or comparison, so it bears on no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: All conditions reach high test accuracy, and the paper reports extended training before grokking for some settings; R1–R4. The records do not establish the full claimed accuracy trajectory or training-set-size dependence.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The reported grokking time decreases from ∼157K steps to ∼25K steps at higher weight decay; R2–R3. The proposed efficiency account and dataset-size prediction are not tested.
